slides.title:
The Problem Statement
• Current physical surveillance systems rely heavily on manual monitoring.
• Existing AI tools in the market are often used in inefficient way.
Research Summary
Integration of face detection, face recognition, and AI features into a real-time web application to automate threat identification and security analytics.
slides.narration:

These cameras can look at lots of people at once and know if anyone should be there or not. By combining this with smart computer programs, we can check for trouble faster and better than just people watching. slides.title:
Security First
Robust authentication and authorization protocols to protect sensitive data.
slides.narration: On this slide, we talk about the importance of having strong security measures in place to protect important information. Imagine you have a treasure chest, and you want to make sure no one can open it without your permission. That’s what we call authentication. It’s like a secret code that you give to people who need to access your information. The slide also mentions something called authorization, which is like deciding who gets to use that secret code. Together, these measures ensure that only the right people can use your data, just like how your parents make sure only you are allowed to open your special toy box. This way, we can keep important information safe and secure.

slides.title:
Case 3: Static Premises
Centrally mounted AI cameras (45° angle) providing 100% automated monitoring of commercial premises.
slides.narration: Let's talk about Case 3: Static Premises. Imagine you have a big store or mall where you want to keep everything safe. We use special cameras called AI cameras. These cameras are placed in one spot, kind of like a watchtower. They can see everything around them and notice any unusual things happening. These cameras are angled at a 45-degree angle, which means they can see a lot of the store without moving. This way, the store can be watched all the time without any need for people to watch it manually. It's like having a security guard but without a human, saving time and money. This makes the store safer for everyone who visits and helps the store owner save money too.

slides.title:
🛡️ Multi-tier Login & Role-based Permissions
🛡️ Email Authentication & Supreme User Auth
🛡️ Sha256 Encrypted Passwords
🛡️ Token-based API Security
🛡️ Encrypted Communication & Data Sanitization
🛡️Usage of RESTful API
slides.narration: On this slide, we're talking about how we secure our system with multi-tiered login and role-based permissions. Imagine you have a toy box, and only certain toys can be played with by certain kids. That's kind of like what we're doing here, but for computer systems. We use email to make sure only the right people can log in. We also use super-strong passwords that are like secret codes, so even if someone finds out your password, they can't break it. Then, we use something called tokens to make sure only the right people get access to certain parts of the system. It's like having a special key that only you know about. And all the information that's being sent back and forth is protected so that no one can read it unless they're supposed to. Finally, we use something called RESTful APIs, which is a way of talking to our system, just like how you might ask your friend if you can borrow their toy. This way, we make sure only the right people can do the right things, keeping everything safe and secure.
